newsitem.title: USA: Texas executes man convicted in 1986 murder.
newsitem.headline: Texas executes man convicted in 1986 murder.

text.p: A Texas man convicted of murdering a convenience store clerk in a 1986 robbery that netted $96 was executed Monday by lethal injection at the Huntsville State Prison.
David Wayne Stoker, 38, was sentenced to die for shooting David Mannrique twice in the back and once in the top of the head during the robbery in Hale Centre, a small town in the Texas panhandle.
"Killing me will not solve anything. The taking of life is never right. I am innocent of murder," Stoker said in a statement released by the prison chaplain after the execution.
Strapped to a gurney in the death chamber as relatives of his victim looked on, Stoker was injected with a dose of lethal chemicals and died shortly after 6 p.m. (2300 GMT).

Stoker admitted to two friends that he killed a store clerk during the November 1986 robbery, and then tried to arrange to have the friends killed to keep them from testifying against him, prosecutors said.

Police said three spent shell casings found in the convenience store were fired from Stoker's handgun, a Ruger .22 calibre automatic that he called "the hot one" and claimed to have used in other shootings.

Stoker spent his final day on death row visiting with relatives and friends, and ordered a last meal of two double-meat cheeseburgers, french fries and ice cream. A last request for cigarettes was refused because smoking is prohibited in the prison here.

Stoker was the 22nd person executed this year and the first of three set to be put to death this week in Texas, which leads the nation with 129 executions since the U.S. Supreme Court reinstated capital punishment in 1976.
